## Meeting notes

### Context — Aurora RFP

Srikantan, Vishakha, and Kishore met to kick off the response to an RFP received from **Aurora Healthcare Network Pvt. Ltd.** earlier this week. Aurora is asking for a Statement of Work (SOW) for a **custom Patient Scheduling & Care Coordination Platform** to replace their ageing in-house system, with implementation, integration with their existing Epic EHR, UAT, deployment, and an initial twelve months of support and maintenance. The RFP attachment (`Aurora-RFP-CareCoordinationPlatform-v1.pdf`) was circulated by Aurora's strategic sourcing lead, **Ramesh Iyer (ramesh.iyer@aurorahealth.in)**, and a response is due in **ten business days**.

Srikantan is the SOW Owner. The internal review will be done by the regional delivery head and the healthcare practice lead before the SOW goes back to Ramesh. The team is treating this as a Tier-1 pursuit — the deal size is meaningful, the customer relationship is new, and healthcare is a strategic vertical for the practice.

- **Customer Position:** Aurora has emphasised three things in the RFP — a fixed go-live target of **end of Q1 next year**, a strong preference for a **milestone-based commercial model**, and a hard requirement that the platform integrate cleanly with their existing **Epic EHR** and their HL7/FHIR partner gateway (labs, imaging). Ramesh has indicated that two other vendors are also responding; price alone will not win it, but a clearly substantiated plan, credible healthcare case studies, and demonstrable FHIR integration experience will.
- **SOW Structure Agreed:** The team agreed the SOW response will be assembled in **four sections**, matching the structure Aurora asked for in their RFP — Technical Proposal, Project Management & Delivery Approach, Commercial Terms, and Relevant Case Studies & Testimonials. Each section needs to be detailed enough that Aurora's evaluation committee can score it without follow-up clarifications.
- **Internal vs External Framing:** Srikantan reminded the team that the internal working draft can carry more candour on risks and assumptions than the version Aurora sees. The team will maintain a single working document and produce the customer-facing version at the end.

### Workstream Assignments

The four SOW sections were assigned with target dates ahead of the internal review on **Day 8** and the customer submission on **Day 10**.

- **Technical Proposal (Vishakha):** Vishakha will own the Technical Proposal section — solution architecture, the proposed tech stack, the Epic EHR (FHIR R4) integration approach, the HL7/FHIR partner-gateway integration for labs and imaging, data migration from Aurora's legacy system, the test strategy, and the deployment / cutover plan. She will draft this as a Word document by **Day 5 EOD**. She flagged that the partner-gateway HL7 message set in the RFP is thin and that she will raise a clarification question to Ramesh in the next two days.
- **Project Management & Delivery (Kishore):** Kishore will own the PM & Delivery section — the proposed delivery methodology (hybrid Agile with milestone gates), the team structure and role mix, the governance cadence, the risk and issue management approach, the change-control process, and the assumptions and dependencies on Aurora. He will produce this as a Word document by **Day 5 EOD**.
- **Commercial Terms (Srikantan):** Srikantan will draft the Commercial Terms section — the milestone-based payment schedule aligned with the RFP's go-live target, the rate card for time-and-materials work beyond scope, the assumptions underpinning the pricing, and the support-and-maintenance pricing for the first twelve months. He will produce this as an Excel pricing model plus a Word narrative, by **Day 6 EOD**.
- **Case Studies & Testimonials (Kishore):** Kishore will pull together three relevant case studies from the practice's reference library — ideally two healthcare-domain engagements (preferably hospital chains) and one Epic / FHIR integration engagement — anonymised where required. He will also collect two written testimonials from prior healthcare clients. Srikantan will review and select the final two case studies that go into the SOW. Target **Day 6 EOD**.
- **Assembled Draft & Reconciliation (Srikantan):** Srikantan will own the final assembled SOW. He will run the cross-section reconciliation — that the timeline in the PM section matches the milestones in the Commercial section, that the team mix in the PM section matches the effort assumed in the Commercial pricing, and that the integration scope in the Technical section is consistent with the assumptions called out in the PM section. Assembled draft for internal review by **Day 7 EOD**.

### Discussion of Customer-Facing Sensitivities

The team discussed what to lean into and what to be careful with in the version that goes to Aurora.

- **HL7 / FHIR Gateway Uncertainty:** Vishakha noted that the RFP is light on the partner-gateway HL7 message-set specifics (which labs, which imaging chains, which message versions) and that the technical assumptions will need to be explicit. The team agreed to call these out clearly in the Technical Proposal's "Assumptions" subsection rather than hide them in the commercial fine print.
- **Patient Data & DPDP Compliance:** Vishakha raised that the platform will handle sensitive patient data under the DPDP Act 2023. The Technical Proposal should explicitly address data residency (India regions only), encryption at rest and in transit, consent management, and right-to-erasure handling. The team agreed this should be a first-class section, not an afterthought in an annexure.
- **Fixed Go-Live Date:** Kishore raised that the end-of-Q1 go-live target is aggressive given the Epic integration surface area and the typical lead times for hospital UAT (clinicians have limited release windows). The team agreed the PM section should propose the date but make the dependencies on Aurora (timely Epic sandbox access, clinician UAT availability, data migration sign-off windows) very explicit, so that any slippage attributable to Aurora is clearly traceable.
- **Pricing Posture:** Srikantan said the commercial posture should be a competitive but defensible milestone-based price, with the support-and-maintenance year priced separately so Aurora can opt in or out without re-opening the build pricing. Both Vishakha and Kishore agreed.

### Internal Review and Customer Submission

The team agreed on the review cadence ahead of the customer submission.

- **Internal Review:** **Day 8** morning, with the regional delivery head and the healthcare practice lead. Srikantan will share the assembled draft the previous evening. Any feedback gets incorporated on Day 8 afternoon and Day 9.
- **Final QA Pass:** **Day 9** afternoon — Srikantan runs a final consistency and tone pass on the customer-facing version.
- **Customer Submission:** **Day 10** before 5pm IST. Srikantan will send the final SOW PDF to Ramesh with Vishakha and Kishore on copy.

## Attachment — Aurora RFP (excerpt circulated with the meeting invite)

> **Request for Proposal — Patient Scheduling & Care Coordination Platform**
> **Issued by:** Aurora Healthcare Network Pvt. Ltd.
> **RFP reference:** AHN-RFP-2026-CARE-009
> **Response due:** Ten business days from issue date
>
> **1. Introduction.** Aurora Healthcare Network ("Client") is seeking software services from a qualified vendor ("Vendor") to design, build, deploy, and support a custom Patient Scheduling & Care Coordination Platform that will replace the Client's existing in-house system. Vendors are requested to respond with a Statement of Work covering the scope, deliverables, timeline, roles, commercials, and relevant credentials.
>
> **2. Objectives.**
> - Deliver a custom platform that meets the functional and non-functional requirements detailed in Annexure A.
> - Integrate the platform with the Client's Epic EHR and the Client's partner-facing HL7/FHIR gateway (labs, imaging).
> - Migrate operational data from the legacy system with zero data loss and documented reconciliation.
> - Provide twelve (12) months of post go-live support and maintenance, priced separately.
>
> **3. Scope of Work (summary — see Annexure A for detail).**
> - 3.1 Software Development — requirements elaboration, design, build, test, documentation, training material.
> - 3.2 Implementation & Deployment — cutover plan, UAT, training, integration with existing infrastructure.
> - 3.3 Support & Maintenance — issue resolution SLAs, patch cadence, periodic audits, dedicated helpdesk, knowledge transfer.
>
> **4. Indicative Timeline.** Go-live target: end of Q1 of the following calendar year. Vendors should propose a milestone plan consistent with this target and call out any dependencies on the Client.
>
> **5. Roles & Responsibilities.** Vendors should propose a delivery team structure, governance cadence, and explicit Client-side responsibilities (system access, UAT participation, sign-off windows).
>
> **6. Commercial Model.** Milestone-based; Vendor to propose the milestone breakdown and payment percentages. Support and maintenance to be priced separately on an annual basis with an option to renew.
>
> **7. Evaluation Criteria.** Technical fit (35%), delivery approach and team (25%), commercials (25%), relevant case studies and credentials (15%).
>
> **8. Submission.** Single PDF response to procurement@aurorahealth.in, c.c. Ramesh Iyer (ramesh.iyer@aurorahealth.in). Clarification questions accepted until Day 5; responses circulated to all bidders.
>
> **— End of RFP excerpt —**
